item.title: Fixed volume and patch test geometries, outward normals and induced orientations
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention already carried by the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ boundary presentations and by the compact $C^1$ surface measure cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ open and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval. This definition fixes the time-independent spatial test geometries of the integral form of the Maxwell equations.

(a) [Volume test geometry] A volume test geometry in $\Omega$ is a pair $(V,\nu_V)$ where $V\subseteq\Omega$ is a nonempty bounded open set with $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ and a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of its boundary ([[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]) and $\nu_V$ is the outward unit normal of that presentation off its edge set ([[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]). The closed-surface flux of a field $F$ continuous on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$ is the finite face sum
$$\oint_{\partial V}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS:=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_V\,dS,$$
with the face surface integrals of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. For every closed axis-parallel box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subseteq\Omega$ with $a_i<b_i$, its open interior $V=\prod_{i<3}(a_i,b_i)$ is a volume test geometry and $\overline V=K$. Its natural six-face presentation is the boundary of $K$, with outward normals $\pm e_i$. The volume variable is $V$, while $K$ denotes its compact closure. Each face is a degenerate three-dimensional box and hence has $\lambda_3$-measure zero by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]]; their finite union $K\setminus V$ is null. Thus for continuous $h$ on a neighbourhood of $K$, $\int_Vh\,d\lambda_3=\int_Kh\,d\lambda_3$: the positive and negative integrals over the null difference vanish by [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] and [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]].

(b) [Patch test geometry] A patch test geometry in $\Omega$ is a regular $C^2$ surface patch $(D,r)$ over a finite elementary Green region in the sense of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]], [[def-admissible-regular-parametrized-surface-patch]]): $D\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ is a finite elementary Green region, $r$ is of class $C^2$ on an open neighbourhood of $D$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]), $r_u\times r_v\ne0$ on the interior of $D$ ([[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) and no interior parameter point shares its image with a distinct point of $D$. Its induced boundary chain $\partial S=r(\partial D)$ and its circulation $\oint_{\partial S}F\cdot d\mathbf r$ for a field continuous on the image are those of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]] ([[def-scalar-and-vector-line-integrals-along-piecewise-c1-paths]]); its oriented flux of a field $F$ continuous on the image is
$$\int_SF\cdot n_S\,dS:=\int_D(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)\,dudv,$$
the scalar Riemann integral of the continuous integrand on the compact Jordan parameter region, in the orientation induced by $r$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). The pair $(D,r)$ is part of the data. Every affine graph patch $r(u,v)=(u,v,\varphi(u,v))$ over an axis-parallel square $D=[c_1,c_1+\ell]\times[c_2,c_2+\ell]$ with $\ell>0$, whose graph lies in $\Omega$ with $\varphi$ affine (for instance constant), and more generally every affine regular patch over such a square, is a patch test geometry: the square is a finite elementary Green region, and $r$ is smooth and regular with $\varphi_u,\varphi_v$ constant.

(c) [Regularity convention] When an integral identity of this framework is asserted for a volume test geometry $V$, respectively for a patch test geometry $S$, with respect to a field $F$ of stated class $C^k$, it concerns fields defined and of class $C^k$ on an open neighbourhood of $\overline V$ in $\Omega$, respectively of the image $r[D]$ in $\Omega$; when the identity involves a time derivative of a flux, the field is defined with the stated regularity on a neighbourhood of that compact set times the compact time interval of the assertion. No regularity away from these neighbourhoods is asserted.

(d) [Conventions and scope] Test geometries are fixed spatial subsets of $\Omega$ and carry no motion. A patch's orientation is the one induced by its parametrization, and its induced boundary chain has the compatible orientation of [[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]], so that the classical Stokes theorem applies with a plus sign. The definition retains the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention of the imported boundary and surface-measure definitions; it asserts no differential equation, no physical law and no existence of fields.
item.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition. Clause (a) composes the imported finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation with its outward normal and the compact-hypersurface face integral; the open box interior, with compact closure $K$, is verified as an instance by listing its six faces (each a compact subset of a regular $C^1$ hypersurface patch, namely a coordinate plane), its twelve edges and eight vertices as the edge set, and noting that the face-edge intersections have surface measure zero and that outside the edges the boundary is locally a coordinate $C^1$ graph with the box on one side. Clause (b) composes the $C^2$ patch over a finite elementary Green region with the induced boundary chain and the oriented patch flux; an affine graph over an axis-parallel square is verified as an instance because a rectangle is both a type $I$ and a type $II$ region with the natural elementary decomposition, so the square carries a finite elementary Green presentation. Clause (c) is a regularity convention recording that all integral identities of this page quantify over fields on neighbourhoods of the compact test sets, which is exactly the hypothesis class of the imported divergence and Stokes theorems. Clause (d) records the orientation and countability conventions and states explicitly that the definition introduces no physical law. Nothing here asserts that every bounded domain is admissible, that a disc is a legal parameter region, or that a physical test geometry is realised by an apparatus. The requirement $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$ makes clause (c)'s existing neighbourhood requirement explicit and restores the canonical definition contract. The closed-box integral bridge follows from the six degenerate faces being volume-null and the signed-integral definition, independently of their nonzero surface areas.

item.title: The Lorentz coupling: external force on a test charge and the continuum force and power densities
item.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
item.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

item.title: Smooth differential-integral equivalence for every admissible test geometry
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the imported piecewise $C^1$ boundary and surface-measure definitions ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; let $E,B$ be fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] on $\Omega\times I$; and let $(V,\nu_V)$ and $(D,r)$ be the volume and patch test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]]. Assume the fields are jointly $C^1$ on $\Omega\times I$ and that the additional derivatives appearing below exist and are continuous there; for instance $E,B$ jointly of class $C^2$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ is sufficient.

(a) [Differential implies integral] If the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, then for every volume test geometry $(V,\nu_V)$ and every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial V}E(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int_V\rho(\cdot,t)\,d\lambda_3,\qquad \oint_{\partial V}B(\cdot,t)\cdot\nu_V\,dS=0,$$
and for every patch test geometry $(D,r)$ the flux functions $t\mapsto\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ and $t\mapsto\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS$ are differentiable on $I$ and, for every $t\in I$,
$$\oint_{\partial S}E(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=-\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS,\qquad \oint_{\partial S}B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r=\mu_0\int_SJ(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS+c^{-2}\frac{d}{dt}\int_SE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_S\,dS.$$

(b) [Integral implies differential] Conversely, suppose the two volume identities of (a) hold for every volume test geometry and every $t\in I$, and that for every patch test geometry the two flux functions are differentiable on $I$ and the two patch identities of (a) hold for every $t\in I$. Then the four smooth-branch equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold pointwise on $\Omega\times I$:
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

The equivalence is asserted for the exact class of test geometries of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], which contains the open interiors of all closed axis-parallel boxes compactly contained in $\Omega$ and the affine square patches; it is not a recovery from one selected volume or one selected patch, and the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] are the operators used.
item.strategy:
(a) Differential implies integral. Fix $t\in I$ and a volume test geometry $V$; $E(\cdot,t)$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$, so [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applies (the theorem assumes the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) and gives $\oint_{\partial V}E\cdot\nu_V\,dS=\int_V\operatorname{div}E\,d\lambda_3=(1/\varepsilon_0)\int_V\rho\,d\lambda_3$ by the Gauss law of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the same computation with $\operatorname{div}B=0$ gives the second identity. For a patch test geometry, [[thm-the-classical-stokes-theorem-for-a-c2-surface-patch]] applied to the $C^1$ fields gives $\oint_{\partial S}E\cdot d\mathbf r=\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS$ with the induced orientation of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and $\int_S\operatorname{curl}E\cdot n_S\,dS=-\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$ by Faraday's law. The flux function is $t\mapsto\int_D\langle B(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle\,dudv$, a Riemann integral over the compact Jordan parameter region of a function whose time derivative $\langle\partial_tB(r(u,v),t),r_u\times r_v\rangle$ is continuous on a neighbourhood of $D$ times a compact interval around $t$; [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this Riemann integral with the Lebesgue integral to which [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] applies, giving differentiability on $I$ with $\frac{d}{dt}\int_SB\cdot n_S\,dS=\int_S\partial_tB\cdot n_S\,dS$. Combining gives the Faraday identity; the Amp\`ere identity is the same with $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$.

(b) Integral implies differential. Fix a point $p\in\Omega$, an index $i$, and the cyclic pair $(j,k)$ with $e_j\times e_k=e_i$. For every closed box $K=\prod_{i<3}[a_i,b_i]\subset\Omega$ with positive sides take its admitted open interior $V$. The volume identities and [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] give $\int_V(\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0)\,d\lambda_3=0$. The integrand $h=\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0$ is continuous on $\Omega$ and bounded on $K$. The six faces of $K\setminus V$ are volume-null by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], so [[cor-integral-over-a-null-set-vanishes]] applied to the positive and negative parts gives $\int_Kh=\int_Vh=0$. In particular this holds for every closed cube $K\subset\Omega$; [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] gives $h=0$ on $\Omega$. The same argument applied to $h=\operatorname{div}B$ gives $\operatorname{div}B=0$. For the curl components, take the affine patch $r(u,v):=p+ue_j+ve_k$ over the square $D_\ell=[-\ell/2,\ell/2]^2$ (a patch test geometry whose parameter region is a rectangle and whose normal is $r_u\times r_v=e_i$); the Faraday identity of (b), Stokes' theorem and the differentiability of the flux function give $\int_{D_\ell}\bigl(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB\bigr)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i\,dudv=0$ for every sufficiently small $\ell>0$. Because the identities hold for every affine square patch contained in $\Omega$, for each fixed coordinate plane every closed square in its open slice is covered (translate its centre to $p$); this is the hypothesis of the planar clause of [[lem-em-coordinate-cell-localization]] for the continuous function $u\mapsto(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)(p+ue_j+ve_k)\cdot e_i$ on the corresponding coordinate plane; hence $(\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB)\cdot e_i=0$ at every point of $\Omega$, for each coordinate $e_i$. The same argument with the Amp\`ere identity gives $(\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE)\cdot e_i=0$. Therefore the four equations hold pointwise. The argument shows why a single selected test geometry is insufficient: the recovery uses the full families of boxes and affine square patches of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]], and the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is exactly the convention of the divergence theorem and the surface-measure interface.

item.title: Transport of flux through a moving patch
item.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$). In the setting of [[def-em-moving-patch]], let $B$ be a $C^1$ field on a neighbourhood of the swept surface with $\operatorname{div}B=0$. Then $\Phi$ is differentiable on $I$ and $$\Phi'(t)=\int_{S(t)}\partial_tB\cdot n\,dS-\oint_{\partial S(t)}(v\times B)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$ the boundary integral using the induced orientation. Without the hypothesis $\operatorname{div}B=0$ the additional term $\int_{S(t)}(v\cdot n)\,\operatorname{div}B\,dS$ appears.
item.strategy: Differentiate the parametrized flux with the parameter lemma; the area derivative contributes $\partial_uv\times r_v+r_u\times\partial_vv$, and collecting terms gives $[\partial_tB+(v\cdot\nabla)B+B\operatorname{div}v-(B\cdot\nabla)v]\cdot(r_u\times r_v)$. The published cross-product identity turns this into $[\partial_tB+v\operatorname{div}B-\operatorname{curl}(v\times B)]\cdot(r_u\times r_v)$, and patch Stokes converts the curl term into the boundary circulation. The $C^2$ hypothesis lets mixed derivatives commute. Lorentz-force interpretation is a separate physical premise.

item.title: Declared material-closure branches: linear nondispersive Ohmic response and the causal memory branch
item.statement:
Adopt as a modelling postulate of this framework the following constitutive branches for the material described by the macroscopic fields of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]].
(a) [Material rest frame] The relations below are stated in a material rest frame: an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the Minkowski model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] ([[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]) in which the material element under consideration is at rest, with spatial basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; when the material is at rest in the laboratory frame of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], the components below are the laboratory components. Boosting the material changes both the fields and the rest observer; this postulate does not assert that the relations below hold with the same constants in every frame.
(b) [Elementary inertial-rest branch] In the rest frame, with constant symmetric positive-definite matrices $\varepsilon,\mu\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ (the isotropic scalar cases $\varepsilon=\varepsilon\mathbf 1$, $\mu=\mu\mathbf 1$ with $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ included), the model takes $$D=\varepsilon E,\qquad B=\mu H,\qquad J_c=\sigma E,$$ where $\sigma\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ is symmetric positive semidefinite and $J_c$ is the conduction part of the free current, $J_f=J_c+J_{\mathrm{ext}}$ for a declared external free current $J_{\mathrm{ext}}$; local, linear and nondispersive (instantaneous) response is part of this restricted assumption. In the isotropic case an exact broadband interpretation of the constant-coefficient law additionally requires $\varepsilon\mu\ge c^{-2}$, so that the characteristic speed $1/\sqrt{\varepsilon\mu}$ does not exceed the vacuum speed $c$; without that condition, and in the anisotropic branch, the constant-coefficient law is a declared finite-band effective phase-response model and carries no universal front-speed claim.
(c) [Causal memory branch] Alternatively, and again in the rest frame, the polarisation response to the electric history is the causal convolution $$P(t)=\varepsilon_0\int_0^\infty K(s)\,E(t-s)\,ds$$ for a declared real matrix kernel $K:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ in $L^1(0,\infty)$ ([[def-l-one-of-a-measure]]); the integral then converges absolutely for bounded continuous histories $E$ because $|K_{jk}(s)E_k(t-s)|\le(\sup|E_k|)|K_{jk}(s)|$. The kernel class actually used, together with causality and passivity, is part of the model and is analysed in [[pthm-em-causal-dispersive-response]]; neither causality nor passivity is automatic. A finitely-subtracted analytic response may instead be declared by a scalar transfer function $\chi$ that is holomorphic on the open upper half-plane, of class $C^1$ on the real boundary away from a real subtraction point $\omega_0$, holomorphic on a neighbourhood of $\omega_0$, and satisfies $|\chi(z)|\le C(1+|z|^{n-1})$ on $\{\operatorname{Im}z\ge0\}$ outside a compact set for some integer $n\ge1$ and constant $C>0$ ([[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]]).
(d) [Status] These are adopted model assumptions, one branch at a time; the framework does not derive them from the vacuum equations or from coarse graining, and no microscopic mechanism, material data or empirical validity is claimed. Ferroelectric and ferromagnetic response, hysteresis, nonlinear response and general nonlocal response lie outside the branches declared here.
item.strategy: An adopted nonproof formulation. The objects are those of [[def-em-polarization-magnetization]]; the macroscopic field equations whose formulation the closure completes are those of [[pthm-em-macroscopic-maxwell]]; the rest-frame notion is the inertial frame of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] used by [[def-em-lab-geometry]], and the memory-branch kernel class is the $L^1$ notion of [[def-l-one-of-a-measure]], whose absolute convergence for bounded continuous histories is the elementary domination displayed in the statement. The finitely-subtracted branch uses the holomorphy notion of [[def-complex-differentiability-holomorphic-and-entire]] and states its growth and boundary hypotheses explicitly rather than hiding them. Clause (d) records that the branches are assumptions with no microscopic or empirical content. No proof is supplied and none is claimed, in accordance with the nonproof status of a postulate; the source and scope review covers the formulation, the rest-frame and scale qualifications and the non-derivation.

item.title: The steady-current (magnetostatic) regime, the compact smooth current class and the declared ideal noncompact models
item.statement:
For the Lebesgue/surface/distributional source and admissibility branches (c)-(d), assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). The smooth formulation in (a) and the smooth conserved-current predicate in (b) do not themselves use Choice. Let the laboratory region and its chart, the field and source objects and the units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]], [[def-em-sources]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and fix $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Steady-current regime] A steady-current (magnetostatic) configuration on $\Omega\times I$ consists of a field pair $E,B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ and source fields $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that are independent of $t$ and satisfy the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] with the operators of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]. For such a configuration the formal distributional branch of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\operatorname{div}J=0$ distributionally; this is pointwise when $J$ is $C^1$. In the jointly $C^2$ field/$C^1$ source branch its classical proof applies directly. The locally integrable distributional reading here inherits Countable Choice, whereas the stated classical $C^2/C^1$ compatibility calculation is choice-free, and the four adopted equations are equivalent to the electrostatic pair and the magnetostatic pair

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J .$$

(b) [Compact smooth current class] The compact smooth current class of this framework consists of the currents $J\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R^3)$ with $\operatorname{div}J=0$, extended by zero to $\mathbb R^3$. A magnetostatic field of such a current is a field $B$ of class $C^1$ on $\mathbb R^3$ satisfying $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ on $\mathbb R^3$ with the extended $J$. This is the hypothesis class of the vector-potential, Biot-Savart and dipole theorems of this page; this definition asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of $B$ in the class.

(c) [Ideal source objects] Define three ideal current source objects outside the compact class, together with the data selecting their fields. (c1) [Closed thin loop] For a closed embedded $C^2$ curve $\gamma:\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R^3$ with $|\gamma'|\equiv1$ ($L>0$) and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal loop current is the distribution $$\langle J_\gamma,\psi\rangle:=I\int_0^L\gamma'(s)\cdot\psi(\gamma(s))\,ds,\qquad \psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3),$$ with $\rho_\gamma:=0$. (c2) [Infinite straight wire] For $\gamma(s)=(0,0,s)$, $s\in\mathbb R$, and $I\in\mathbb R$, the ideal wire current is $\langle J_{\rm w},\psi\rangle:=I\int_{\mathbb R}\psi_3(0,0,s)\,ds$, with $\rho_{\rm w}:=0$. (c3) [Infinite cylindrical sheet] For $a>0$, $S=\{\rho=a\}$, $\rho=\sqrt{x_1^2+x_2^2}$, and $K\in\mathbb R$, the ideal solenoid sheet current is $\langle J_S,\psi\rangle:=K\int_S e_\varphi\cdot\psi\,dS$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], read on compact cylinder segments), with $\rho_S:=0$. All three pairings are finite because $\psi$ has compact support. (c4) [Admissibility] A field $B$ is admitted for one of these declared models when: $B$ is locally integrable on $\mathbb R^3$ (hence a distribution by [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]) and $C^1$ off the support of the current; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ hold pointwise off that support; the distributional identities $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J$ hold against every scalar divergence test $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and vector curl test $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R^3)$ in the sense of [[def-distributional-derivative]]; $B$ has the model's declared symmetry (invariance under translations along and rotations about the axis in (c2) and (c3); no symmetry is required in (c1)); and $B$ obeys the decay requirement: $|B(x)|\to0$ as $|x|\to\infty$ in (c1), and in (c2), (c3) the supremum of $|B|$ over every compact set of cross-sectional parameters tends to $0$ as the transverse radius $\rho\to\infty$. The companion examples exhibit and verify the fields of the two axisymmetric models in this class; the definition itself asserts no existence, uniqueness, finite energy or limiting relation for the declared models, and no compact-class theorem of this page applies to them.

(d) [Scope] This is a model restriction: the steady-current regime for compact smooth currents, and three explicitly declared ideal noncompact or singular models. It excludes point charges, weaker-regularity volume sources, moving sheets, normal sheet currents and any claim of empirical exactness; the equations in (c4) define a mathematical admissibility predicate; its physical adoption for these source objects is a separate postulate, and no product of distributions is formed.
item.strategy: Formulation and well-definedness checks. Clause (a) reduces the existing smooth Maxwell equations by setting every time derivative to zero; the continuity consequence is the formal distributional branch of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]], or its smooth branch under its exact jointly $C^2$ field/$C^1$ source hypotheses. No pointwise divergence of a merely continuous current is asserted. Clause (b) defines the compact conserved smooth class. The pairings (c1)-(c3) are continuous linear functionals: on a fixed compact test support, their absolute values are bounded by $|I|L\|\psi\|_\infty$, $|I|$ times the finite length of its axis projection times $\|\psi\|_\infty$, or $|K|$ times the finite area of a containing compact cylindrical face times $\|\psi\|_\infty$, respectively. The cylinder chart $X(\theta,z)=(a\cos\theta,a\sin\theta,z)$ has Gram density $a$; finitely many angular charts cover each compact face and define its measure by [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. Thus the source functionals have order zero. In (c4), divergence acts on scalar tests and curl on vector tests under [[def-distributional-derivative]]. Admissibility, symmetry and decay are predicates, not an assertion of existence or a physical law. No equation for these excluded singular source objects is inferred from the older point/compact-sheet postulate. Countable Choice is inherited by the compact-face surface and regular-distribution interfaces. Full physical use of these source objects requires the separate same-page adoption postulate.

item.title: Coulomb-gauge Newtonian vector potential for a compact smooth conserved current
item.strategy: **Proof technique:** componentwise reduction to the Newtonian-potential lemma and the standard second-derivative vector identities. 1.1 For each $i$ the datum $J_i$ is smooth and compactly supported, so [[lem-em-smooth-newtonian-upgrade]] gives $A_i=\mu_0N(J_i)\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $D^\alpha A_i=\mu_0N(D^\alpha J_i)$ for every multi-index $\alpha$ and $-\Delta A_i=\mu_0J_i$ pointwise ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]); hence (a). 2.1 Take $\alpha=e_i$ in the same derivative identity. Since $\operatorname{div}J=\sum_i\partial_iJ_i=0$ and $N$ is componentwise linear, $$\operatorname{div}A=\sum_i\partial_iA_i=\mu_0\sum_iN(\partial_iJ_i)=\mu_0N(\operatorname{div}J)=0$$ pointwise ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); this is (b), and $\operatorname{div}J=0$ is used nowhere else. 3.1 $B=\operatorname{curl}A$ is $C^\infty$ because $A$ is. Then $\operatorname{div}B=\operatorname{div}\operatorname{curl}A=0$ by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]], and $$\operatorname{curl}B=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A=\nabla(\operatorname{div}A)-\Delta A=\mu_0J$$ by [[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]] combined with (b) and (a). This is the pointwise magnetostatic pair of (c). 3.2 Reading (c) inside the framework: [[def-em-steady-current-regime]](a) identifies the magnetostatic pair as the reduction of the adopted equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] when $\partial_tE=\partial_tB=0$, with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: choose $E=\rho=0$ and extend $B,J$ independently of time; the electrostatic identities and both time derivatives then vanish. Alternatively a given compatible electrostatic pair supplies them. No unspecified electric field or charge density is being asserted to exist (the identity $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ is not used in this item). 3.3 (d) is scope bookkeeping: the gauge freedom and homogeneous solutions are not analysed here, and no claim is extended beyond the compact smooth class. Countable Choice is inherited through the cited measure, surface, regular-distribution and/or Newtonian supplier interfaces; no stronger choice axiom is used in this argument.

item.title: Capacitance and energy for specified linear conductor geometry
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice for the cited unit-Dirichlet solvability and trace interfaces, and its Countable Choice consequence for surface and integral interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(\Omega;D_1,\dots,D_m;\Omega_v)$ be the conductor geometry of [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]], additionally with $\Omega$ a bounded $C^\infty$ ambient domain and $\Omega_v$ connected and with the **outer boundary $\partial\Omega$ grounded**: the data on $\partial\Omega$ are the constant Dirichlet datum $0$; let $\rho_v\equiv0$ on $\Omega_v$ (the pure capacitor configuration: no volume source), and let the framework constants be those of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. For each $j\in\{1,\dots,m\}$ let $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be the unit-potential solution of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) with the smooth data
$$\varphi_j|_{\partial D_k}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \varphi_j|_{\partial\Omega}=0,$$
so that $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ on $\Omega_v$ with the Laplacian of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], and let $\nu$ be the outward normal of $\Omega_v$ (so on $\partial D_j$ the normal $\nu$ points into the conductor). Define the **capacitance matrix** by
$$C_{jk}:=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi_k}{\partial\nu}\,dS,\qquad j,k=1,\dots,m,$$
the flux integrals of continuous functions over the compact embedded hypersurfaces $\partial D_j$ (normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]]) ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]). Then:
(a) [Linearity and matrix form] for every $V=(V_1,\dots,V_m)\in\mathbb R^m$ the unique equilibrium potential with conductor potentials $V$ and grounded outer boundary is $\varphi^V=\sum_{j=1}^mV_j\varphi_j$, and the conductor charges of [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d) are
$$Q_j(V)=\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial D_j}\frac{\partial\varphi^V}{\partial\nu}\,dS=\sum_{k=1}^mC_{jk}V_k,\qquad\text{i.e.}\qquad Q=CV.$$
(b) [Reciprocity] $C$ is symmetric: $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ for all $j,k$; the symmetry is Green's symmetric pairing of the harmonic potentials $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$.
(c) [Energy identity] the field energy of the configuration is
$$U(V)=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\Omega_v}|\nabla\varphi^V|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac12V^{T}CV=\frac12\sum_{j=1}^mV_jQ_j(V),$$
and $U(V)>0$ for every $V\ne0$: $C$ is symmetric positive definite. In particular $U(V)\ge0$, with equality exactly for $V=0$, so every nonzero conductor-potential data set stores positive field energy.
(d) [Two-conductor reading] with only conductor $1$ driven and every other conductor grounded, $V=te_1$: $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $Q_j=C_{j1}t$ for $j\ne1$, and $U=\tfrac12C_{11}t^2=\tfrac12Q_1V_1=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; the **capacitance of the arrangement** at conductor $1$ with respect to the grounded reference is the positive geometric number $C_{11}>0$, with $C_{11}=Q_1/V_1$ when $t=V_1\ne0$, and the energy identities $U=\tfrac12QV=Q^2/(2C)=\tfrac12CV^2$ hold with $C=C_{11}$, $Q=Q_1$, $V=V_1$. By (c) the positivity holds for every diagonal entry, $C_{jj}>0$.
(e) [Assembly reading] use the family $V_j(s)=sV_j$, $\varphi_s=s\varphi^V$, $Q_j(s)=sQ_j(V)$ for $0\le s\le1$, with fixed geometry and grounded reference. Prescribe the quasistatic external charge-transfer work by $dW_{\rm ext}=\sum_jV_j(s)dQ_j(s)$. Then $W_{\rm ext}=\int_0^1s\,ds\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=U$. The potentials vary during assembly; only the final potentials and geometry are fixed. This derives the sheet-charge accounting directly and does not apply the volume-source theorem [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]] to singular sheets. The family is an accounting prescription, not an asserted time-dependent Maxwell/material solution.
(f) [Scope] the theorem assumes: the compact separated conductor geometry, the additional bounded smooth ambient domain, and connected vacuum region of the model, the grounded outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, zero volume source, and the existence and uniqueness of the unit-potential Dirichlet solutions ([[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c), [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a)). It asserts no solvability for arbitrary boundary data (the existence theorem is used only for the constant data above), no prescribed-total-charge problem, no dielectric or material response, no finite-conductivity or transient charging dynamics, no radiation, and no measurement; the matrix $C$ is a geometric object of the ideal electrostatic model, and the ideal parallel-plate and similar formulas are statements about this model only.
item.strategy:
Use the additional bounded smooth ambient hypothesis with the separated compact body closures to obtain a bounded smooth vacuum by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]]. The general open ambient branch alone supplies no bounded Dirichlet solver. Existence of each $\varphi_j$: the pure electrostatic regime is [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]; the datum that is $\delta_{jk}$ on $\partial D_k$ and $0$ on $\partial\Omega$ is constant, hence smooth, on each compact boundary piece of the disjoint union $\partial\Omega_v$, so [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-existence]](c) gives $\varphi_j\in C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with $-\Delta\varphi_j=0$ and those boundary values. (a) Linearity: $\sum_jV_j\varphi_j$ is a $C^\infty(\overline{\Omega_v})$ function with $-\Delta igl(\sum_jV_j\varphi_j igr)=0$ and boundary values $V_k$ on $\partial D_k$, $0$ on $\partial\Omega$; by the Dirichlet uniqueness of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-bvp-uniqueness]](a) it is the unique equilibrium potential with those data, and the charges are obtained by substituting into the flux formula of [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d): the integral is linear in $\varphi$, giving $Q_j(V)=\sum_kC_{jk}V_k$. (b) Green's first identity on the bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega_v$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], applied twice and subtracted) gives, for the harmonic $\varphi_j,\varphi_k$,
$$0=\int_{\Omega_v} igl(\varphi_j\Delta\varphi_k-\varphi_k\Delta\varphi_j igr)d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v} igl(\varphi_j\partial_
u\varphi_k-\varphi_k\partial_
u\varphi_j igr)dS;$$
the outer boundary contributes zero because both potentials vanish there, and on the conductor surfaces $\varphi_j=\delta_{j\ell}$, so the sum over components $D_\ell$ reduces to $\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_
u\varphi_k-\int_{\partial D_k}\partial_
u\varphi_j$, i.e. $C_{jk}=C_{kj}$ after multiplying by $\varepsilon_0$. (c) Apply Green's first identity once more with $u=v=\varphi^V$:
$$\int_{\Omega_v} igl(\varphi^V\Delta\varphi^V+|
abla\varphi^V|^2 igr)d\lambda_3=\int_{\partial\Omega_v}\varphi^V\partial_
u\varphi^V\,dS.$$
The Laplacian term vanishes, the outer boundary contributes $0$, and on $\partial D_j$ the trace of $\varphi^V$ is the constant $V_j$, so the boundary integral equals $\sum_jV_j\int_{\partial D_j}\partial_
u\varphi^VdS=\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)/\varepsilon_0$ by [[pthm-em-conductor-surface-charge]](d); multiplying by $\varepsilon_0/2$ gives $U(V)=	frac12V^TCV$. Positivity: $
abla\varphi^V$ is continuous on the compact $\overline{\Omega_v}$, hence Borel and bounded, and $|
abla\varphi^V|^2$ is integrable with finite integral ([[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]); $U(V)\ge0$ because the integrand is nonnegative. If $U(V)=0$ then $\int|
abla\varphi^V|^2=0$, hence $
abla\varphi^V=0$ $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere by [[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]], hence $
abla\varphi^V=0$ everywhere by continuity, hence $\varphi^V$ is constant on the connected open set $\Omega_v$ ([[thm-zero-derivative-on-connected-open-euclidean-set-iff-constant]]); the constant is $0$ because $\varphi^V=0$ on the nonempty boundary $\partial\Omega$ and $\varphi^V$ is continuous on the closure; finally $V_j=\varphi^V|_{\partial D_j}=0$ for every $j$. Thus $C$ is positive definite and in particular symmetric with positive diagonal. (d) is the case $V=te_1$ of (a) and (c): $Q_1=C_{11}t$, $U=	frac12C_{11}t^2=	frac12Q_1V_1$, and eliminating $t=Q_1/C_{11}$ gives $U=Q_1^2/(2C_{11})$; $C_{11}>0$ is (c) with $V=e_1$. (e) Linearity gives $\varphi_s=s\varphi^V$, $V(s)=sV$, $Q(s)=sQ(V)$ and hence the surface density scales by $s$. Moving an infinitesimal charge $dQ_j$ from the grounded reference at zero potential to conductor $j$ has electric-force work $-V_j(s)dQ_j$, so the balancing quasistatic external contribution is $+V_j(s)dQ_j$. Prescribing this charge-transfer accounting and summing gives $\sum_jV_j(s)dQ_j(s)=s\,ds\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)$. Integrate $s$ from zero to one to obtain $W_{m ext}=	frac12\sum_jV_jQ_j(V)=U$. All signs of charges and voltages are admitted. The reference is grounded throughout but the driven potentials vary with $s$; external support is assumed. This is derived for the surface charges and not imported from the smooth volume-source hypothesis of [[pthm-em-electrostatic-field-energy]]. (f) lists the hypotheses: only constant boundary data are solved, so no claim of arbitrary-boundary solvability or of charge-data solvability is made, and no material, radiative or empirical content is introduced. For (d), handle $t=0$ first: $\varphi^V=0$, all charges vanish and $U=0$, while $C_{11}$ is still defined by its unit-potential flux and is strictly positive. Only for $t
e0$ is the ratio $Q_1/V_1$ formed. Full AC is inherited solely through the unit Dirichlet/trace solvability suppliers; all subsequent finite linearity and energy calculations add no stronger assumption. The continuous nonnegative energy density can vanish almost everywhere only by vanishing everywhere in the open vacuum: a nonzero value would stay bounded below on a small Euclidean ball of positive measure ([[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). The endpoint work calculation uses the known global potential directly: [[thm-gradient-theorem-for-line-integrals]] gives $\int_\gamma E_s\cdot dr=\varphi_s({m start})-\varphi_s({m end})$ on each interior piecewise $C^1$ path, and boundary endpoints are limits using the continuous closure traces. It does not apply the star-shaped existence hypotheses of the earlier electrostatic-work theorem to a conductor vacuum with holes. The charge-transfer family is prescribed bookkeeping, and no actual particle/source dynamics is inferred.

item.title: Euclidean balls, annuli and spheres as bounded smooth domains and hypersurfaces
item.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the boundary-chart and surface-measure interfaces used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). On $\mathbb R^3$ with its Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) let $0<\varepsilon<R$ and put
$$B_R:=\{x:|x|<R\},\qquad \overline B_R:=\{x:|x|\le R\},\qquad A_{\varepsilon,R}:=\{x:\varepsilon<|x|<R\},\qquad S_r:=\{x:|x|=r\}.$$
Then:
(a) [Domains] $B_R$ and $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ are bounded $C^1$ domains in the sense of [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]; their boundaries are $S_R$, respectively $S_\varepsilon\cup S_R$, and the corresponding outward unit normals are
$$\nu(x)=\frac{x}{|x|}\ \ (x\in S_R),\qquad \nu(x)=-\frac{x}{|x|}\ \ (x\in S_\varepsilon,\ \text{boundary of }A_{\varepsilon,R});$$
(b) [Spheres] each $S_r$ is a compact embedded $C^1$ (indeed $C^\infty$) hypersurface in the sense of [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] with two-sided unit normals $\pm x/|x|$, and the boundary components $S_\varepsilon,S_R$, each subdivided into six compact signed-maximal-coordinate graph faces $F_{r,k,\sigma}:=\{x\in S_r:\sigma x_k\ge |x_j|\text{ for all }j\}$ ($k=1,2,3$, $\sigma=\pm1$), with the compact edge set consisting of their seams $\sigma x_k=|x_j|$ for $j\ne k$, give a finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation of $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ in the sense of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]];
(c) [Consequences used downstream] the divergence theorem and Green's first identity of [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] and [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] apply on $B_R$ and on $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ with the outward normals of (a), and $S_r$ carries a finite Borel surface measure with the standard graph charts.
item.strategy: The continuous norm makes $B_R$ and $A_{\varepsilon,R}$ nonempty bounded open sets, and radial perturbations show their boundaries are respectively $S_R$ and $S_\varepsilon\cup S_R$ ([[thm-continuity-preimage-characterisation]], [[def-metric-interior-closure-boundary]], [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]). Here is an explicit finite graph cover of a sphere $S_r$. For $k=1,2,3$ and $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ use the relatively open patch $\sigma x_k>r/(2\sqrt3)$; these six patches cover because some $|x_k|\ge r/\sqrt3$. In rigid coordinates $(y,z)$ with $z=\sigma x_k$, each patch lies on the positive graph $z=h(y)=\sqrt{r^2-|y|^2}$. Around each point choose a graph cylinder small enough that $z>0$, $|y|<r$ and any other annulus boundary is absent. The sphere is exactly this graph, and the ball is exactly $z<h(y)$ there. In particular reflection of a lower physical hemisphere yields the positive graph $+\sqrt{r^2-|y|^2}$, not the negative graph. The chain and power rules make $h$ smooth on $|y|<r$ ([[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]]). For the inner boundary of the annulus the domain is locally the complement of $\overline B_\varepsilon$. Starting with $z=\sigma x_k>0$, reflect once more to $w=-z$; the graph is $w=-h(y)$ and the exterior condition $z>h(y)$ becomes exactly the required subgraph $w<-h(y)$. The outer boundary uses the ball chart. The definition's graph normal $(-Dh,1)/\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$, with $Dh=-y/h$, transports to $x/r$ for the ball/outer sphere. For the complement chart $g=-h$, its graph normal is $(-Dg,1)/\sqrt{1+|Dg|^2}=(-y,h)/r$ in $(y,w)$; transport by $w=-\sigma x_k$ gives $-x/r$, the annulus inner normal. Hence (a) and its signs follow from [[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Each sphere is closed and bounded, hence compact by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]], and the six smooth graph patches make it a compact embedded smooth hypersurface with two-sided normals. For the finite piecewise presentation, subdivide each sphere component into the six compact Borel faces $F_{r,k,\sigma}$ of (b). They cover $S_r$. On each face $\sigma x_k\ge r/\sqrt3$, so the whole face is contained in the one regular positive graph patch $z=\sigma x_k=\sqrt{r^2-|y|^2}$ with $z>r/(2\sqrt3)$. The parameter set of that face is compactly contained in $|y|<r$. Define $E$ to be the finite union, for $r=\varepsilon,R$, of the seams where two or more coordinates have tied maximal absolute value. This is compact and contains every relative face boundary and every distinct-face overlap. In the chart of $F_{r,k,\sigma}$ any seam is contained in $h(y)=|y_j|$ for one of the two other coordinates $j$, hence satisfies $y_j=\pm\sqrt{(r^2-y_\ell^2)/2}$ with $\ell\ne j,k$. For each fixed $y_\ell$ this has at most two $y_j$ values, so its Borel parameter set has planar Lebesgue measure zero by [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] and [[prop-degenerate-boxes-and-coordinate-hyperplanes-are-lebesgue-null]]. Its chart density $\sqrt{1+|Dh|^2}$ is bounded on the compact face, so it also has zero chart surface measure by [[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]] and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]. Away from $E$ the already established smooth domain chart is a single graph and the normals are exactly the outward ones computed above. These twelve faces and their null seam set satisfy every requirement of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]]. The divergence theorem and first Green identity apply to these domains with precisely those normals ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], [[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). The compact chart surface carries finite Borel measure by [[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]]. The only choice cost is the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of that interface. The seam indicator is Borel, and the planar Euclidean/Borel product identification needed for that Fubini argument is [[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]] with [[thm-lebesgue-product-measure-agrees-with-euclidean-lebesgue-on-borel-sets]].
